meta.how_to_use: Stages PP1-PP10 build the full portal; stages PW1-PW5 build the compact Workshop PWA. The recommended order (build_order) runs the compact app right after the foundation and the onboarding wizard, so phone-only workshops can join the pilot early. Backend needs are listed in backend_requests with the same entry shape as the other frontend plans and join backend/BR-update-plan.json through its intake rules. When a proposal is accepted, set its status and record the decision in progress_log.

global_decisions.decision: One business app, two surfaces. The full provider portal and the compact Workshop PWA are route groups of the same Next.js business app at web.<DOMAIN> (WP20), with the same BFF and OAuth client cp-web-portal, the same generated contract, the same design system and i18n. The Workshop PWA lives under /<locale>/workshop/ with its own web app manifest (scope /<locale>/workshop/, start_url /<locale>/workshop/today, name 'CarPal Workshop' / «کارپال تعمیرگاه»), so it installs as its own home-screen app on the phone.
global_decisions.why: SEC-WEB-5 keeps {org} operations out of the consumer BFF, and Docs/90 line 124 keeps business notifications out of the consumer app. One app means components built once (request card, pre-visit report, reply editor, showcase composer) serve both surfaces.
global_decisions.alternative: PRV-OQ-01 (host it inside the consumer PWA like the fleet driver view /<locale>/drive).

global_decisions.decision: The Workshop PWA does three jobs only: (1) review and answer appointment requests, (2) reply to customers (review replies, review approval answers, comments on the shop's showcases and posts), (3) post before/after photos. Plus what those need: sign-in, business picker, Today screen, notifications and web push, language, theme. Every other task shows as 'Open in full portal' (same session, same tab) and is never re-implemented in the compact app.
global_decisions.why: Owner scope 2026-11-15. A short list keeps the app small enough for low-end phones and quick to learn.

global_decisions.decision: The server decides everything. Both surfaces show actions from Appointment.allowed_transitions, the caller's role (P* sees, P+ publishes replies and showcases, per Docs/40 sec lines) and plan entitlements (ENT(ai_tools_enabled) for AI drafts). The client never keeps its own copy of a rule; a 403 becomes 'Ask the owner' for staff roles.
global_decisions.why: Same rule as the fleet ?fleet option in frontend/README.md: the compact surface only hides pages.

global_decisions.decision: Phone-first budgets for the Workshop PWA: first-load JS for /workshop routes ≤ 120 KB gzip, LCP ≤ 2.5 s on a mid-range phone over throttled 4G, Sunlight theme offered on first run and followed automatically with prefers-contrast: more, 48 px targets, one primary action per screen, no maps loaded (a static address line instead). Photos are resized in the browser to ≤ 2048 px long side and re-encoded (WebP or JPEG, ≈ ≤ 600 KB) before media.upload_init; uploads resume through the media.upload_* steps while the page is open.
global_decisions.why: Docs/carpal-design-system: workshop yards, sun, greasy hands, mobile data.

global_decisions.decision: Camera through <input type=file accept=image/* capture=environment>, not getUserMedia, so SEC-WEB-4 (camera allowed only on the consumer origin) needs no change. The service worker caches the app shell only, never API answers (they carry PII: pre-visit reports, customer contact), and is wiped at sign-out, as in pwa P12.
global_decisions.why: Keeps the business origin's security headers as the contract states them.

global_decisions.decision: AI output is always a labelled draft (AI suggestion chip). The owner edits and publishes; nothing AI-written is sent or published by the client without a human tap. When AI is off (flag or plan), the same screens work with empty editors and the category picker.
global_decisions.why: Docs/11 Ch.2 and Ch.8 ('AI suggests, provider approves'), Docs/40 ai.* descriptions.

screens.name: Sign in
screens.content: Mobile number, one-time code (autocomplete one-time-code), passkey when the browser supports it, 'Keep me signed in on this phone'. No sign-up form: 'New business? Set up in the full portal'.

screens.name: Install and notifications
screens.content: First run: business picker (provider organizations only), Sunlight theme offer, Add to Home Screen (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen steps, needed for iOS web push), 'Get new requests on this phone' push permission after the user taps it.

screens.name: Today
screens.content: Counters for new requests (with oldest age and average response time), replies waiting (reviews without reply, approval requests with days left, unanswered comments), photos waiting for customer approval; today's confirmed appointments as a short list; Verification pending banner; safety-critical requests first.

screens.name: Requests
screens.content: Segments New · Proposed · Upcoming; cards with vehicle, problem line, urgency, preferred time, request age, safety mark; pull to refresh.

screens.name: Request detail
screens.content: Customer display name and 'first visit'; vehicle and mileage; AI pre-visit summary (labelled) or 'Triage: not provided'; photos and video; shared history or 'Not shared by customer'; preferred times; AI slot suggestion with the day's load ('2 of 2 lifts busy 09:00-12:00'); coverage mismatch note; sticky action bar Accept · Propose time · More (Decline, Ask for information).

screens.name: Answer sheets
screens.content: Accept: pick one of the customer's windows or a time, duration (AI suggestion prefilled). Propose time: date and time chips for the next 14 days, note to the customer. Decline: reason chips (fully booked, don't work on this car, don't offer this service, other + text). Ask for information: message to the customer (customer-visible note), status stays provider_reviewing.

screens.name: Replies
screens.content: Tabs Reviews · Comments · Approvals with counts; review cards with stars, confirmation label (Verified visit / Approved by the business and CarPal), excerpt, 'No reply yet'; comment cards with the showcase thumbnail; approval cards with days left.

screens.name: Reply to a review
screens.content: Full review and context; AI draft (labelled, tone chips Friendly · Formal · Brief) in an editable box; risk note from the AI ('No liability or legal sensitivity detected'); Publish reply; Save draft; 'Flag or request mediation' opens the full portal.

screens.name: Reply to a comment
screens.content: The showcase or post card, the comment thread, a reply box that posts as the shop (Shop badge), Report comment.

screens.name: Approval request
screens.content: 'Do you recognise this customer?' with display name, date and kind of work only; Yes, this was our customer · I don't recognise this customer · Not sure (ask CarPal); note visible to CarPal only; days left; rule text 'A low rating is never a reason to say no'.

screens.name: Photos
screens.content: Grid of showcases with status (Draft, Waiting for customer, Being reviewed, Live, Declined), New before/after button, 'Jobs ready for photos' (recently completed appointments).

screens.name: New before/after
screens.content: Step 1 pick the job (completed appointment; vehicle and service filled in). Step 2 Before photos and After photos, each from camera or gallery, up to 10, upload progress per photo.

screens.name: Check and caption
screens.content: AI pairs before/after (swap), flags plates and faces with Blur (default on) and Keep, caption draft and tags (vehicle, system, task) as editable chips, cover photo choice.

screens.name: Send for customer approval
screens.content: Preview as the customer will see it; 'Ask Sara M. to approve' (provider.portfolio_consent_request); optional 'Also share to the feed' when the community flag is on; result screen with the status and what happens next.

screens.name: Update job / Close job (proposed, PRV-OQ-02)
screens.content: Status buttons from allowed_transitions (In progress, Awaiting parts with note and estimate, Ready for pickup) and Close job: service system and task prefilled, final cost, warranty note, invoice photo. Parts used and cost breakdown stay in the full portal.

build_order.why: PP1 and PP2 are needed by every provider (no shop can exist without onboarding). The Workshop PWA then delivers the daily loop (request → reply → photos) to phone-only workshops early. Its shared components (request card, pre-visit report, reply editor, showcase composer, upload kit) are built in PW stages inside src/features/provider/ and get their desktop layouts in PP3, PP5 and PP6.
pilot_blockers_outside_this_plan: Web push sender in the backend (pwa DI-72 / OQ-26): without it the Workshop PWA falls back to polling while open, email, and SMS where enabled; the 'phone buzzes' promise of Docs/11 Ch.5 is not met.
PRV-BR-01..03 for comment replies as the shop (PW3 ships reviews and approvals without them, comments when they land).

backend_requests.for: PW3, PP6 (reply to comments as the shop)
backend_requests.request: comments.create accepts as_organization_id (caller must be an active P*/V* member of that organization; allowed on targets owned by that organization, and on questions and answers like AnswerWrite), and Comment carries author_organization: PublicOrgCard | null so pages can show the Shop badge.
backend_requests.why: Docs/22 W-PUB-05 promises 'provider replies with Shop badge', but comments.create is USR only and Comment has no organization author: a reply today would appear under Reza's personal display name.

backend_requests.request: GET {org}/comments (ORG(P*, V*)): comments on the organization's posts and portfolio items, newest first, with target summary (type, id, title, cover thumbnail), replied_by_org: boolean, and filters unreplied and target.
backend_requests.why: The shop cannot see new comments without opening every showcase; comments.list needs a target id.

backend_requests.request: Comment threading one level deep: parent_comment_id on create and in Comment, so a shop reply attaches to the customer's comment.
backend_requests.why: CommentTarget only allows post, portfolio_item, question and answer; a reply cannot point at the comment it answers.

backend_requests.request: Notification events for the organization: comment.created on the organization's content (to P+ members, respecting preferences), and confirm that appointment.requested, review.published, review.approval.requested (+ day 3 and day 6 reminders) and portfolio consent answers notify the provider members with the deep-link targets of this plan.
backend_requests.why: The Workshop PWA lives on pushes; Module L lists 'new inquiry' and requests but not comments on the shop's content.

backend_requests.request: Structured decline reasons: AppointmentTransition to cancelled from the provider side takes decline_reason_code ('fully_booked'|'vehicle_not_covered'|'service_not_offered'|'other') and an optional note shown to the customer.
backend_requests.why: Docs/40 says 'provider decline = cancelled with reason "declined"', which leaves no room for the reason the customer and the matching need (Docs/11 Ch.5 'Decline requires a reason').

backend_requests.request: Web push sender with a VAPID key pair (pwa DI-72, OQ-26) and the portal's own VAPID public key for web.<DOMAIN>.
backend_requests.why: Without a sender the Workshop PWA cannot buzz the phone for a new request.

backend_requests.request: provider.portfolio_consent_request for a job without a CarPal appointment: by email or SMS to a contact the shop enters, with a cn link and the same consent page, rate-limited like review invitations.
backend_requests.why: Today the consent request needs appointment_id or service_record_id, so a walk-in job can never become a public showcase (Docs/11 open point 6).

doc_issues.issue: Docs/90 and Docs/02 WP20 have no compact provider app. Add the Workshop PWA (screens PW-*, scope PRV-GD-02) to Docs/90 §6 and to WP20 once accepted.
Publish vs verification (Docs/11 open point 5): Docs/56 §2.10 requires an active business to publish, §2.11 allows 'Verification pending'. This plan follows §2.11.

Docs/90 P-TEAM-01 lists roles Owner, Manager, Service advisor, Mechanic limited view, Marketing/review responder; Docs/40 has provider_owner, provider_manager, provider_staff; Docs/11 uses owner, bookings, technician. The WP0 matrix must settle one list (Docs/11 open point 4).
Docs/11 open points 8 (review approval screen) and 10 (map statistics in Insights) are now covered by Docs/90 P-REV-04 and P-INS-01 'Map & search visibility'. Close them in Docs/11.
Docs/11 open points 1-3 (job log, provider parts search, trade accounts) get the new screen ids P-JOB-01, P-PART-01, P-PART-02 in PP9; Docs/90 needs their specs.

open_questions.question: Where does the Workshop PWA live: a route group of the business app at web.<DOMAIN>/<locale>/workshop (cp-web-portal), or a 'shop mode' inside the existing consumer PWA at pwa.<DOMAIN>, like the fleet driver view /<locale>/drive?
open_questions.default: The business app (PRV-GD-01). It keeps business operations and pushes out of the consumer BFF (SEC-WEB-5, Docs/90 line 124) and shares components with the full portal.
open_questions.trade_off: The consumer PWA option could ship sooner, because its BFF, upload kit, service worker and push are already built, and Reza would have one app for his family car and his shop. But it widens the consumer BFF to {prv} writes and puts business pushes in the consumer app, against both rules above.

open_questions.question: Add a minimal 'Update job / Close job' (PW-JOB-01) to the Workshop PWA?
open_questions.default: Yes, as part of PW2. Without completion there is no service record, no Verified visit review, no review invitation and no evidence (Docs/11 Ch.7-8), so a phone-only workshop would never earn badges. Parts used and the cost breakdown stay in the full portal.
open_questions.trade_off: It goes past the three jobs the owner named.

open_questions.question: How does a workshop without a computer onboard: the full portal's wizard on the phone (responsive), a compact wizard inside the Workshop PWA, or staff-assisted onboarding only?
open_questions.default: The full portal's wizard, tested at 360 px (PP2), with staff-assisted onboarding from the console as the alternative (PU-P01). A separate compact wizard would be a second copy of eight steps.

open_questions.question: cp-web-portal sessions end after 8 h idle (Docs/40 §2.2). On a phone app used every morning this means signing in daily. Keep it, or give the installed Workshop PWA a longer idle time?
open_questions.default: Keep 8 h idle / 7 days absolute and make re-sign-in one tap with a passkey (offered after the second code sign-in). A longer lifetime is a security-model change in Docs/40.

open_questions.question: Offline queue for photos taken without signal (IndexedDB), or uploads only while the page is open?
open_questions.default: Only while open in the MVP (the admin console's no-Web-Storage rule also avoids photos with plates lingering on a shared phone); resumable upload steps cover short drops. Revisit after the pilot.

open_questions.question: Can a showcase be made from a walk-in job that had no CarPal appointment (customer approves by an emailed or SMS link)?
open_questions.default: No in the MVP: PW4 offers only completed CarPal appointments, which also pushes shops to use Request. PRV-BR-07 is the path if the answer is yes.

open_questions.question: Does 'replying to consumer comments' cover comments on the shop's showcases and posts (as this plan assumes), besides review replies? And appointment messages ('Ask for information' and the customer's answer)?
open_questions.default: Review replies, review approvals and comments on the shop's content are in PW3. Appointment messages stay inside the request detail (PW2), not in Replies.

open_questions.question: Name and screen-id prefix: 'CarPal Workshop' / «کارپال تعمیرگاه» with ids PW-*?
open_questions.default: Yes; WP0 approves the prefix as it did W- for the consumer web.

open_questions.question: Is the iOS limit acceptable for the pilot: web push on iPhone works only after Add to Home Screen (iOS 16.4+)? Or plan a native business app (Docs/11 open point 9)?
open_questions.default: Acceptable for the pilot (Android dominates the target market); PW-SYS-01 walks iPhone users through Add to Home Screen. Re-check after the pilot.
